page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory subsystem consists of 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates solid compute performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1926.0 and a multi-core score of 7695.0. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly at 32.73 GB/sec, and text processing in Geekbench also registers a strong score of 2743.0. However, memory-intensive operations show some limitations; the Passmark memory score of 1800.86 is categorized as weak, and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth drops to 47.98 GB/sec.

The c7i.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory allocations or local storage. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it is optimized for raw processing density rather than memory-intensive databases. While it handles smaller language model inference adequately—achieving 154.29 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model—performance drops significantly to 6.32 tokens/sec on a 7B model, highlighting its limitations for larger AI workloads. This instance is designed for compute-bound tasks such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and moderate-scale batch processing.
